proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  Assignment positivity makes \(q_a\) well defined.  Consistency gives
\[
 q_a=P(W_a=1\mid A=a),
\]
and randomization then gives \(q_a=P(W_a=1)\).  Put \(p_a=P(Y_a=1)\).  If either event \(\{Y_a=y\}\) has probability zero, its joint contribution below is zero; otherwise the corresponding shared-channel conditional equality may be multiplied by \(P(Y_a=y)\).  Thus the law of total probability, shared sensitivity, and shared specificity give
\[
\begin{aligned}
q_a
 &=P(W_a=1,Y_a=1)+P(W_a=1,Y_a=0)\\
 &=s p_a+(1-c)(1-p_a)\\
 &=v p_a+u(1-p_a)=u+(v-u)p_a.
\end{aligned}
\]
The Youden-floor assumption gives \(v-u=d\geq\kappa>0\), so division is valid and
\[
 p_a=\frac{q_a-u}{v-u}.
\]
Because the denominator is positive, \(0\leq p_a\leq1\) is equivalent to \(u\leq q_a\leq v\).  Imposing this simultaneously for \(a=0,1\), together with the channel rectangle and \(v-u\geq\kappa\), gives exactly
\[
 u_L\leq u\leq\min(u_U,q_0,q_1),\qquad
 \max(v_L,q_0,q_1)\leq v\leq v_U,
 \qquad v-u\geq\kappa,
\]
which is the definition of \(D\).  This proves necessity.  Conversely, if \((u,v)\in D\), the displayed fractions lie in \([0,1]\).  Choose Bernoulli variables with these two margins (for example, independently), generate each \(W_a\) conditionally with success probability \(u+(v-u)Y_a\), randomize \(A\) independently with positive arm probabilities, and impose consistency.  The resulting law has observed risks \(q_a\) and the required common channel.  This proves sufficiency and hence the claimed equivalence.

Fix \((u,v)\in D\).  By assay inversion, \(p_0,p_1\in[0,1]\).  For a proposed benefit mass \(b=p_{01}\), the margin equations and total mass force
\[
 (p_{00},p_{01},p_{10},p_{11})=(1-p_0-b,b,b-\Delta,p_1-b),
 \qquad \Delta=p_1-p_0.
\]
All four coordinates are nonnegative exactly when
\[
 b\in J:=\bigl[\max(0,\Delta),\min(p_1,1-p_0)\bigr].
\]
The interval is nonempty because \(\max(0,p_1-p_0)\leq p_1\) and \(\max(0,p_1-p_0)\leq1-p_0\).

The cross-product equality is equivalent to
\[
 F(b):=\theta b(b-\Delta)-(p_1-b)(1-p_0-b)
      =r b^2+(1-r\Delta)b-p_1(1-p_0)=0,
 \qquad r=\theta-1.
\]
At the lower endpoint of \(J\), either \(b=0\) or \(b-\Delta=0\), and hence \(F\leq0\).  At the upper endpoint, either \(p_1-b=0\) or \(1-p_0-b=0\), and hence \(F\geq0\).  Since \(F\) is a polynomial, let \(b_*\) be the supremum of the nonempty set of points in \(J\) where \(F\leq0\).  Polynomial continuity shows that neither \(F(b_*)<0\) nor \(F(b_*)>0\) is possible, so \(F(b_*)=0\).

For every \(b\in J\), writing the four displayed nonnegative cell masses gives
\[
 F_b(b)=\theta(p_{01}+p_{10})+p_{11}+p_{00}
 \geq \min(\theta,1)(p_{00}+p_{01}+p_{10}+p_{11})
 =\min(\theta,1)>0.
\]
Thus \(F\) is strictly increasing on \(J\), and \(b_*\) is the unique feasible root.  If \(\theta=1\), then \(r=0\) and the equation gives \(b_*=p_1(1-p_0)=C\).  If \(r\neq0\), completing the square gives
\[
 (2rb_*+B)^2=B^2+4rC,
 \qquad B=1-r\Delta,
 \qquad C=p_1(1-p_0).
\]
Moreover \(2rb_*+B=F_b(b_*)>0\).  Therefore the positive square-root sign is forced and
\[
 b_*=\frac{-B+\sqrt{B^2+4rC}}{2r}=b_{\theta}(u,v).
\]
The membership \(b_*\in J\) proves nonnegativity of all four masses; their sum is one by direct addition.  Finally, \(F(b_*)=0\) is precisely
\[
 p_{11}p_{00}=\theta p_{10}p_{01}.
\]
This also covers structural-zero contacts because only nonnegativity, not division by a cell probability, was used.

Write
\[
F(b;p_0,p_1,\theta)=\theta b(b-p_1+p_0)-(p_1-b)(1-p_0-b).
\]
For any convergent sequence of arguments in \([0,1]^2\times[\theta_L,\theta_U]\), every subsequential limit of the corresponding feasible roots satisfies the limiting equation and lies in the limiting Fr\'echet interval.  The uniqueness lemma therefore forces every such limit to be the limiting compatible root.  Hence \(b_{\theta}\) is continuous, including at structural-zero contacts and at \(\theta=1\).

At a point where differentiation is taken, the unique-root proof gives the strictly positive denominator
\[
 F_b=\theta(p_{01}+p_{10})+p_{11}+p_{00}>0.
\]
Direct partial differentiation at fixed \(b\) yields
\[
 F_{\theta}=p_{01}p_{10},\qquad
 F_{p_0}=\theta p_{01}+p_{11},\qquad
 F_{p_1}=-(\theta p_{01}+p_{00}).
\]
Solving \(F_b,db+F_t,dt=0\) for each coordinate \(t\) gives
\[
 \frac{\partial b}{\partial\theta}
 =-\frac{p_{01}p_{10}}{\theta(p_{01}+p_{10})+p_{11}+p_{00}},
\]
\[
 \frac{\partial b}{\partial p_0}
 =-\frac{\theta p_{01}+p_{11}}{\theta(p_{01}+p_{10})+p_{11}+p_{00}},
 \qquad
 \frac{\partial b}{\partial p_1}
 =\frac{\theta p_{01}+p_{00}}{\theta(p_{01}+p_{10})+p_{11}+p_{00}}.
\]
Every numerator is nonnegative.  The denominator minus the numerator of \(-\partial b/\partial p_0\) is \(\theta p_{10}+p_{00}\geq0\), and the denominator minus the numerator of \(\partial b/\partial p_1\) is \(\theta p_{10}+p_{11}\geq0\).  Consequently
\[
 \frac{\partial b}{\partial\theta}\leq0,qquad
 -1\leq\frac{\partial b}{\partial p_0}\leq0,qquad
 0\leq\frac{\partial b}{\partial p_1}\leq1.
\]
Integrating these signs along coordinate segments in the interior gives the three asserted monotonicities.  Approximating a boundary segment by interior segments and using the already-proved continuity extends them, and the derivative inequalities, to boundary contacts.  The same integration also gives, for fixed \(\theta\),
\[
 |b(p_0,p_1,\theta)-b(p'_0,p'_1,\theta)|
 \leq |p_0-p'_0|+|p_1-p'_1|.
\]
No positivity beyond that used to make \(F_b>0\) is required.

Put \(x=q_0\), \(y=q_1\), \(\delta=y-x\), and \(d=v-u\).  The channel polygon \(D\) is a closed rectangle intersected with one closed half-plane.  It is therefore compact and convex, and it has at most five vertices.  For fixed \(\theta\), multiply the root equation by \(d^2>0\) to obtain
\[
 H(u,v,b)=r d^2b^2+(d-r\delta)d b-(y-u)(v-x)=0.
\]
The unique-root lemma gives
\[
 H_b=d^2\{\theta(p_{01}+p_{10})+p_{11}+p_{00}\}>0.
\]
Thus along every line segment in \(D\), implicit differentiation is legitimate away from an endpoint, including when \(\theta=1\).

First exclude unlisted interior extrema.  If \(x\neq y\), the map \((u,v)\mapsto(p_0,p_1)\) has Jacobian determinant
\[
 \det\frac{\partial(p_0,p_1)}{\partial(u,v)}=\frac{y-x}{(v-u)^3}\neq0.
\]
At an interior channel, all four compatible cells are positive: both margins are strictly between zero and one, and a finite positive \(\theta\) places the unique root strictly inside its Fr\'echet interval.  Hence the two margin derivatives in the comparative-statics lemma are respectively strictly negative and strictly positive.  Their gradient cannot be annihilated by an invertible Jacobian, so no interior stationary point exists.  If \(x=y=q\), then \(p_0=p_1=p\), and the equation becomes
\[
 rb^2+b=p(1-p),\qquad
 \frac{db}{dp}=\frac{1-2p}{1+2rb}.
\]
The denominator equals the positive root derivative.  The only interior stationary set is therefore \(p=1/2\), equivalently \(u+v=2q\), and on it
\[
 b=\frac{1}{2(1+\sqrt\theta)}.
\]
If this ridge meets \(D\), the endpoints of its intersection with the compact polygon lie on the boundary and are listed by the candidate rule: they are stationary-line contacts on axis-aligned edges or the single central contact on the informativeness edge.

It remains to classify each boundary edge.  Direct differentiation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
H_u&=-2rdb^2-(2d-r\delta)b+v-x,\\
H_v&= 2rdb^2+(2d-r\delta)b-(y-u),\\
H_u+H_v&=u+v-x-y.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(r\neq0\), elementary polynomial elimination of \(b\) gives the factorizations
\[
\operatorname{Res}_b(H,H_u)
=-r^2d^2(v-x)(v-y)\{\theta\delta^2-(u+v-x-y)^2\},
\]
\[
\operatorname{Res}_b(H,H_v)
=-r^2d^2(u-x)(u-y)\{\theta\delta^2-(u+v-x-y)^2\}.
\]
These identities follow by expanding the two quadratic--linear resultants; hence a common zero makes the displayed product zero.  On a horizontal edge, stationarity in its varying \(u\)-coordinate requires \(H_u=0\); away from a margin contact all prefactors are nonzero, so
\[
 u+v=x+y\pm\sqrt\theta\,|y-x|.
\]
The identical conclusion follows on a vertical edge from \(H_v=0\).  When \(r=0\), direct differentiation of
\[
 b=\frac{(y-u)(v-x)}{(v-u)^2}
\]
gives
\[
 b_u=\frac{(v-x)(2y-u-v)}{(v-u)^3},
 \qquad
 b_v=\frac{(y-u)(2x-u-v)}{(v-u)^3};
\]
the two stationary lines are \(u+v=2y\) and \(u+v=2x\), exactly the preceding formula at \(\theta=1\).

The excluded margin-contact edges have no hidden extremum.  If \(x\leq y\), then on \(u=x\) one has \(b=(y-x)/(v-x)\), and on \(v=y\) one has \(b=(y-x)/(y-u)\); each is monotone along the edge.  If \(y\leq x\), then on \(u=y\) or \(v=x\) one has \(b=0\).  Equal-risk contact edges likewise have \(b=0\).  Their extrema are therefore at vertices.  Finally, on \(v=u+\kappa\), implicit differentiation and the formula for \(H_u+H_v\) give
\[
 \frac{d}{du}b_{\theta}(u,u+\kappa)
 =-\frac{2u+\kappa-x-y}{H_b}.
\]
There is at most one stationary point, and it is the listed point \(u+v=x+y\).  Vertices cover the remaining endpoints.  The same one-dimensional argument covers a segment, and a singleton is itself a vertex.  This proves candidate completeness.

For the count, intersecting a rectangle with the half-plane \(v-u\geq\kappa\) produces at most five vertices.  Each of the two distinct-or-coincident slope \(-1\) stationary lines intersects the boundary of a convex polygon in at most two points; because it cannot coincide with an axis-aligned or slope \(1\) edge, it contributes at most two axis-edge contacts.  The informativeness edge contributes at most one further stationary point.  After duplicates are removed,
\[
 |C_{\theta}|\leq5+4+1=10.
\]
If the informativeness cut is absent, the feasible polygon is a rectangle, so the corresponding count is \(4+4=8\).

The comparative-statics lemma profiles the odds coordinate: the minimum over \(\theta\in[\theta_L,\theta_U]\) is at \(\theta_U\), and the maximum is at \(\theta_L\).  Candidate completeness and the definition of \(L,U\) therefore identify the extrema of the continuous root map over \(D\times[\theta_L,\theta_U]\).

It remains to prove sharpness rather than merely an outer bound.  For every \((u,v,\theta)\) in that domain, the unique-root lemma makes the four masses in the attaining-law definition nonnegative, summing to one, and satisfying
\[
 p_{11}p_{00}=\theta p_{10}p_{01},
\]
which implies the closed cross-product band.  Conditional Bernoulli generation of \(W_a\) gives sensitivity \(v=s\) and specificity \(1-u=c\); independent randomization and consistency give the observed risks by assay inversion.  Hence every root value is attained by a law in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}\).  Conversely, every law in that model supplies a channel in \(D\), and its closed band supplies some \(\theta\in[\theta_L,\theta_U]\): if \(p_{10}p_{01}>0\), take \(\theta=p_{11}p_{00}/(p_{10}p_{01})\); if the product is zero, the closed inequalities force \(p_{11}p_{00}=0\), so any band value gives the equality.  Uniqueness then makes its benefit equal to the compatible root.

Finally, any two domain points are joined by a line segment in the convex set \(D\times[\theta_L,\theta_U]\).  Along that segment the root is continuous.  The supremum construction used in the unique-root proof, applied to the continuous scalar path, shows that every value between its endpoint values is taken.  Joining minimizers and maximizers therefore shows that the attainable image is exactly \([L,U]\).  This proves both sharpness and endpoint attainment by the stated construction.

Assume \(D^{\circ}\neq\varnothing\), and fix \(z^{\circ}\in D^{\circ}\).  Since \(D\) is convex, for every \(z\in D\) and \(0<t\leq1\),
\[
 z_t=(1-t)z+t z^{\circ}\in D^{\circ}.
\]
Indeed, the two strict inequalities defining \(D^{\circ}\) hold for \(z_t\) because they hold at \(z^{\circ}\) and weakly at \(z\).  Thus \(D^{\circ}\) is dense in \(D\).  A channel lies in \(D^{\circ}\) exactly when both corrected margins lie in \((0,1)\).  For finite \(0<\theta<\infty\), the sign argument in the unique-root proof is then strict at both Fr\'echet endpoints, so the compatible root is strictly inside that interval and all four cells are positive.  Conversely, four positive cells force both margins into \((0,1)\).  Hence \(D^{\circ}\times[\theta_L,\theta_U]\) is precisely the channel--odds domain generating \(\mathcal M_+\).

Continuity and density now give
\[
 \inf_{\mathcal M_+}b=min_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}}b=L,
 \qquad
 \sup_{\mathcal M_+}b=max_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}}b=U.
\]
For attainment of the lower endpoint, suppose first that some \(z\in C_{\theta_U}\cap D^{\circ}\) satisfies \(b_{\theta_U}(z)=L\).  The attaining-law construction has four positive cells by the preceding paragraph and therefore belongs to \(\mathcal M_+\); this proves sufficiency.  Conversely, suppose a strict law attains \(L\).  Its four cells are positive, so
\[
 \frac{\partial b}{\partial\theta}<0.
\]
Consequently its odds coordinate must equal \(\theta_U\).  Its channel is a minimizer in \(D^{\circ}\).  If \(q_0\neq q_1\), the finite-envelope proof excludes an interior stationary channel.  A strict boundary minimizer cannot lie on a marginal-contact edge; on an axis-aligned edge it is a vertex or a stationary-line contact, and on the informativeness edge it is a vertex or its unique stationary point.  It is therefore in \(C_{\theta_U}\cap D^{\circ}\).  If \(q_0=q_1\), the only additional possibility is the ridge \(u+v=2q_0\); its intersection with \(D\) has a boundary representative with the same value, and every point on that ridge has corrected margins \(p_0=p_1=1/2\), so that representative remains in \(D^{\circ}\) and belongs to the candidate map.  Degenerate polygon cases use the same edge argument.  Necessity follows.  Replacing minimum by maximum and \(\theta_U\) by \(\theta_L\) proves the upper-endpoint criterion.

If \(s=c=1\), then \(u=0\), \(v=1\), and assay inversion gives \(p_a=q_a\).  Substitution in the unique quadratic therefore gives the fixed-clean-margin binary odds reconstruction.  If also \(\theta_L=\theta_U=1\), then \(r=0\), and the unique-root formula becomes
\[
 b=p_1(1-p_0).
\]

For the stated synthetic box, \(u\leq1/10<q_0<q_1<4/5\leq v\), and the smallest possible channel difference is \(4/5-1/10=7/10\).  Thus every point of the rectangle is feasible whenever \(\kappa\leq7/10\), and the informativeness cut is redundant.  At \(\theta=4\), the stationary-line sums are
\[
 q_0+q_1\pm2|q_1-q_0|=\frac{3}{10},\frac{7}{10},
\]
both below the rectangle's minimum sum \(1/20+4/5=17/20\).  Hence the lower endpoint is found by checking the four vertices.  In lexicographic order
\[
 (u,v)\in\{(1/20,4/5),(1/20,9/10),(1/10,4/5),(1/10,9/10)\},
\]
their \(\theta=4\) root values are
\[
 -\frac1{10}+\frac{\sqrt{89}}{30},\qquad
 \frac{10}{51},\qquad
 -\frac2{21}+\frac{2\sqrt{10}}{21},\qquad
 \frac{\sqrt{193}-5}{48}.
\]
Squaring after moving the positive rational terms to the other side verifies that the last is no larger than each of the first three.  Thus the smallest value occurs at \((u,v)=(1/10,9/10)\), where
\[
 p_0=\frac18,qquad p_1=\frac14,qquad
 96b^2+20b-7=0.
\]
The unique feasible root is therefore
\[
 L=\frac{\sqrt{193}-5}{48}.
\]
At \(\theta=1\), the stationary-line sums are \(2q_0=2/5\) and \(2q_1=3/5\), again below the rectangle.  In the same order, the four vertex values are
\[
 \frac4{15},\qquad\frac{70}{289},\qquad\frac{12}{49},\qquad\frac7{32}.
\]
Cross multiplication shows that \(4/15\) is the largest.  It occurs at \((u,v)=(1/20,4/5)\), where \(p_0=1/5\), \(p_1=1/3\), and hence
\[
 U=p_1(1-p_0)=\frac4{15}.
\]
The corresponding cell vectors, in \((00,01,10,11)\) order, are
\[
 \left(\frac{47-\sqrt{193}}{48},
       \frac{\sqrt{193}-5}{48},
       \frac{\sqrt{193}-11}{48},
       \frac{17-\sqrt{193}}{48}\right)
\]
and
\[
 \left(\frac8{15},\frac4{15},\frac2{15},\frac1{15}\right).
\]
Since \(11<\sqrt{193}<14<17\), every displayed cell is positive.  Direct multiplication verifies the respective cross-product equalities at \(\theta=4\) and \(\theta=1\), so both bounds are attained by positive-cell laws.

For each primitive, let \(E_0,E_1,E_s,E_c\) denote the event that its Clopper--Pearson interval contains its true probability.  The cited exact-coverage result and the four marginal binomial assumptions give
\[
 \Pr(E_0^c)\leq\beta_0,\quad
 \Pr(E_1^c)\leq\beta_1,\quad
 \Pr(E_s^c)\leq\beta_s,\quad
 \Pr(E_c^c)\leq\beta_c.
\]
The pointwise indicator inequality
\[
 \mathbf 1_{(E_0\cap E_1\cap E_s\cap E_c)^c}
 \leq \mathbf 1_{E_0^c}+\mathbf 1_{E_1^c}
      +\mathbf 1_{E_s^c}+\mathbf 1_{E_c^c}
\]
and the confidence-budget assumption imply
\[
 \Pr(E_0\cap E_1\cap E_s\cap E_c)\geq1-\beta.
\]
No independence was used.  On this event, validation transport and channel compatibility put the true tuple \((q_0,q_1,u,v)\) in \(\widehat{\mathcal F}\).  Hence, for every \(\theta\in[\theta_L,\theta_U]\), its compatible root is in the projected image \(I_{\beta}\).  Monotonicity in \(\theta\) shows that their image is precisely
\[
 K^{\star}=[b_{\theta_U}(u,v),b_{\theta_L}(u,v)],
\]
so \(K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}\).  The argument is pointwise for every compatible law and therefore proves the displayed infimum coverage.  It involves no uniqueness of an optimizer, differentiability of a moving face, or positive dimension of the feasible polytope; ties, contacts, and collapsed faces are consequently covered.

It remains to expose the promised finite computation.  Write \(Q_a=[\ell_a,h_a]\), and let \(R\) be the rectangle obtained by intersecting the validation intervals with the fixed channel rectangle and changing coordinates from \(c\) to \(u=1-c\).  A channel admits some feasible trial risks exactly when it belongs to
\[
 D_Q=R\cap\{u\leq\min(h_0,h_1),\ v\geq\max(\ell_0,\ell_1),\ v-u\geq\kappa\}.
\]
For a fixed channel, the margin monotonicities profile the risks as
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc|c}
&\widetilde q_0&\widetilde q_1&\theta\\ \hline
\text{lower endpoint}&\min(h_0,v)&\max(\ell_1,u)&\theta_U\\
\text{upper endpoint}&\max(\ell_0,u)&\min(h_1,v)&\theta_L.
\end{array}
\]
For the lower endpoint, a feasible channel with \(v\leq h_0\) makes \(p_0=1\), while one with \(u\geq\ell_1\) makes \(p_1=0\); in either case \(b=0\).  Feasibility of these two clipped polygons is an exact finite linear check.  If neither exists, all of \(D_Q\) has \(v>h_0\) and \(u<\ell_1\), so the risks are fixed at \((h_0,\ell_1)\) and the ten-point theorem computes the lower endpoint.

For the upper endpoint, split \(D_Q\) by the two lines \(u=\ell_0\) and \(v=h_1\).  On the four closed regions the profiled objective is, respectively,
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
u\leq\ell_0,\ v\geq h_1&b_{\theta_L}(\ell_0,h_1;u,v)\\
u\geq\ell_0,\ v\geq h_1&(h_1-u)/(v-u)\\
u\leq\ell_0,\ v\leq h_1&(v-\ell_0)/(v-u)\\
u\geq\ell_0,\ v\leq h_1&1.
\end{array}
\]
The first region uses the ten-point map and the last needs only a feasibility check.  On either fractional region the denominator is at least \(\kappa>0\).  If a polygon point is \(z=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i\), where \(z_i\) are its vertices, then a ratio of affine numerator \(N\) and positive affine denominator \(G\) satisfies
\[
 \frac{N(z)}{G(z)}
 =\sum_i\frac{\lambda_iG(z_i)}{\sum_k\lambda_kG(z_k)}
       \frac{N(z_i)}{G(z_i)}.
\]
It is thus a convex combination of its vertex values, so its extrema occur at vertices.  This proves the four-region rule, including all shared boundaries by harmless duplication.

For the kill-test data, the lower profile fixes
\[
 \widetilde q_0=0.4000678118,qquad
 \widetilde q_1=0.3318863111,qquad
 \theta=0.9016929770.
\]
The point \((u,v)=(0.0395824405,0.4886211008)\) lies in the calibration rectangle, satisfies both margin inequalities, and has
\[
 v-u=0.4490386603>\kappa=0.4490386602.
\]
It is the retained vertex where the left channel edge meets the informativeness boundary to the displayed input precision.  Substitution in the stable quadratic formula gives
\[
 p_0=0.802793619282\ldots,qquad
 p_1=0.650954798424\ldots,qquad
 b=0.132058055576\ldots.
\]
Equivalently, treating every displayed input as its terminating decimal rational, substitution into \(F\) gives opposite signs at \(0.1320580555\) and \(0.1320580556\), while \(F_b>0\); hence the root lies between them.  Thus the projected lower search necessarily retains \(0.1320580555\) to the displayed truncation precision.

We first derive a deterministic modulus.  Along any segment joining two compatible primitive tuples \(\eta=(q_0,q_1,u,v)\) and \(\eta'=(q'_0,q'_1,u',v')\), the linear compatibility inequalities and \(v-u\geq\kappa\) remain valid.  For
\[
 p_a=\frac{q_a-u}{v-u}
\]
direct differentiation gives
\[
 \left|\frac{\partial p_a}{\partial q_a}\right|=\frac1d,qquad
 \left|\frac{\partial p_a}{\partial u}\right|=\frac{v-q_a}{d^2}=\frac{1-p_a}{d},qquad
 \left|\frac{\partial p_a}{\partial v}\right|=\frac{q_a-u}{d^2}=\frac{p_a}{d}.
\]
All three are at most \(1/\kappa\).  Combining segment integration with the root's unit margin Lipschitz bound yields, uniformly in \(\theta\),
\[
 |b(\eta,\theta)-b(\eta',\theta)|
 \leq\frac{|q_0-q'_0|+|q_1-q'_1|+2|u-u'|+2|v-v'|}{\kappa}.
\]
Since \(|u-u'|=|c-c'|\) and \(|v-v'|=|s-s'|\), this is the asserted weighting of the four primitive coordinates.

Next bound each Clopper--Pearson interval.  If \(X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N,p)\) and \(Q_\gamma(X)=[L_X,U_X]\) is its two-sided interval, an interior upper endpoint satisfies the defining lower-tail equation \(\Pr_{U_X}(X'\leq X)=\gamma/2\).  When \(U_X>X/N\), the cited Hoeffding inequality gives
\[
 \frac\gamma2\leq\exp\{-2N(U_X-X/N)^2\},
\]
and hence
\[
 U_X-X/N\leq\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\gamma)}{2N}}.
\]
The lower endpoint follows from the other tail; boundary endpoints \(0\) and \(1\) satisfy the corresponding one-sided claim directly.  Therefore
\[
 Q_\gamma(X)\subseteq
 \left[X/N-\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\gamma)}{2N}},
       X/N+\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\gamma)}{2N}}\right]\cap[0,1].
\]

On the simultaneous primitive-coverage event from the exact-projection theorem, both a feasible projected coordinate and the truth lie in the same primitive interval.  Their coordinate differences are therefore at most \(2\varepsilon_j\).  The deterministic modulus gives, for every feasible projected tuple and every \(\theta\),
\[
 |b(\widetilde\eta,\theta)-b(\eta^{\star},\theta)|
 \leq R:=\frac2\kappa\sum_jw_j\varepsilon_j.
\]
The true tuple is itself feasible on this event, so exact projection gives the first inclusion.  Taking the infimum and supremum over projected tuples in the last display gives
\[
 K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}
 \subseteq[\inf K^{\star}-R,\sup K^{\star}+R]\cap[0,1].
\]
The event has probability at least \(1-\beta\), and no independence among counts entered either this step or the union bound.

For the expectation claim, let \(\widehat p_j\) denote the four empirical proportions and define
\[
 R_{\mathrm{data}}=\frac1\kappa
 \sum_jw_j\bigl(|\widehat p_j-p_j^{\star}|+\varepsilon_j\bigr).
\]
The interval containment just proved shows, without conditioning on primitive coverage, that every coordinate in a primitive interval is within \(|\widehat p_j-p_j^{\star}|+\varepsilon_j\) of the truth.  The modulus therefore implies, taking the length of an empty projection to be zero,
\[
 \{\operatorname{length}(I_{\beta})-
       \operatorname{length}(K^{\star})\}_{+}
 \leq2R_{\mathrm{data}}.
\]
For a binomial empirical proportion,
\[
 E|\widehat p_j-p_j^{\star}|
 \leq\sqrt{E(\widehat p_j-p_j^{\star})^2}
 =\sqrt{\frac{p_j^{\star}(1-p_j^{\star})}{N_j}}
 \leq\frac1{2\sqrt{N_j}}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \sup_P E_P\{\operatorname{length}(I_{\beta})-
       \operatorname{length}(K^{\star})\}_{+}
 \leq\frac2\kappa\sum_jw_j
 \left\{\frac1{2\sqrt{N_j}}+\varepsilon_j\right\}
 =O\!\left(\frac1{\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}}}\right)
\]
when the four marginal budgets are fixed.  Every bound is uniform in the compatible primitive probabilities.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N,p)\), where \(N\geq1\), \(p\in[0,1]\), and \(0<\gamma<1\).  The two-sided equal-tailed Clopper--Pearson interval with total noncoverage \(\gamma\), obtained by inversion of the two binomial tails, contains \(p\) with probability at least \(1-\gamma\).

proposed.statement: For every law satisfying the shared sensitivity and specificity equalities with \(d\ge\kappa\), the latent margins obey \(p_a=(q_a-u)/(v-u)\). A channel is probability-compatible if and only if it belongs to \(D\).
proposed.justification: The common channel couples the two corrected margins, so its exact feasible polygon is the first nonseparable object.
proposed.gap: Molinari2008 gives a general linear channel system; this lemma specializes it to one common binary assay and records the exact joint compatibility polygon.
proposed.consumer: The polygon is the feasible domain used by every endpoint and confidence-projection calculation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The observed arm risk equals the marginal recorded potential-outcome risk only after randomization is used; the replacement declares that load-bearing dependency without changing the claim.

proposed.statement:
Under assignment positivity, the four marginal binomial sampling laws, validation transport, and the confidence-budget condition,
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}}\Pr_P\{K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}\}\ge1-\beta.
\]
No mutual-independence condition on \(T_0,T_1,V_1,V_0\) is required. Coverage holds uniformly through optimizer ties, marginal contacts, and collapsed faces. Moreover, each endpoint of \(I_{\beta}\) is computable by a four-region profiling rule: the nontrivial root region uses the ten-point map, the two fractional regions use polygon vertices, and the constant region uses a feasibility check. Applied to \(\mathrm{def:kill-test-witness}\), the lower projection retains the legal edge value \(0.1320580555\) to the displayed precision.
proposed.justification: Exact primitive inversion avoids branchwise bootstrap failures and remains valid at every nonsmooth contact.
proposed.gap: GabrielSachsJensen2024 evaluates bootstrap coverage, documents regular-bootstrap undercoverage near boundaries, and reports a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) correction; FanPark2010 and KaidoMolinariStoye2019 provide adjacent clean-bound and generic projection inference. None gives exact simultaneous validation-binomial projection through the finite contact-complete shared-assay evaluator.
proposed.consumer: A prospective BNT162b2-style endpoint study with a blinded validation substudy obtains a uniformly valid confidence set for its full true-channel benefit interval.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The coverage proof invokes exact Clopper--Pearson coverage, so the cited theorem is added explicitly to the proof spine without changing the claim.

proposed.statement:
Under assignment positivity, let \(N_j=(n_0,n_1,m_1,m_0)\), \(w_j=(1,1,2,2)\), and \(\varepsilon_j=\sqrt{\log(2/\beta_j)/(2N_j)}\). Uniformly over compatible primitives with \(d\ge\kappa\), with probability at least \(1-\beta\),
\[
K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}\subseteq[\inf K^{\star}-R,\sup K^{\star}+R]\cap[0,1],\qquad R=\frac{2}{\kappa}\sum_jw_j\varepsilon_j.
\]
In addition, \(\sup_P E_P[\{\operatorname{length}(I_{\beta})-\operatorname{length}(K^{\star})\}_{+}]=O(1/(\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}}))\) for fixed marginal budgets. These claims use only the four marginal binomial laws and do not require their counts to be mutually independent.
proposed.justification: Coverage alone can be vacuous; the width theorem quantifies the statistical price of weak assay informativeness and four primitive intervals.
proposed.gap: KaidoMolinariStoye2019 establishes uniform asymptotic coverage for generic moment projections but not an exact finite-sample width modulus indexed by the Youden floor.
proposed.consumer: Validation-study designers can translate a desired benefit-interval precision into trial and gold-standard stratum sizes.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The interval-radius proof invokes Hoeffding's binomial deviation inequality, so the cited theorem is added explicitly to the proof spine without changing the claim.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A matching lower bound for \(M^{\star}\), and therefore the exact minimal universal cap, remains open.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen handle does not define the admissible algorithm or information model behind a required channel evaluation. A configuration with ten distinct candidate incidences does not imply that all ten objective values must be queried, because algebraic dominance tests may discard candidates without evaluation. Thus a no-smaller-cap claim is not well typed from the present primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: The boundary arrangement was reduced to at most five vertices, four stationary-line contacts, and one informativeness-edge contact. Realizable incidence patterns can make all ten locations distinct, but that only lower-bounds the cardinality of the unpruned candidate set, not the query complexity of every exact endpoint procedure.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The finite-envelope proof establishes the computable upper bound \(M^{\star}\leq10\) for direct evaluation of the declared candidate map, and \(M^{\star}\leq8\) when the informativeness cut is absent.  Ten distinct candidate incidences are realizable.  For example, take
\[
 [u_L,u_U]=[0,2/5],\quad [v_L,v_U]=[1/2,1],\quad
 \kappa=3/10,\quad (q_0,q_1)=(21/50,12/25),\quad \theta=16.
\]
Then \(D\) is the pentagon with vertices
\[
 (0,1/2),(1/5,1/2),(2/5,7/10),(2/5,1),(0,1).
\]
The stationary sums are \(33/50\) and \(57/50\), giving the four distinct axis-edge contacts
\[
 (0,33/50),(4/25,1/2),(2/5,37/50),(7/50,1),
\]
while the central informativeness-edge contact is \((3/10,3/5)\).  None coincides with a vertex, and the whole polygon is strictly compatible because \(u\leq2/5<21/50\) and \(v\geq1/2>12/25\).  This realizes ten candidate locations while preserving strict compatibility.  It still does not prove that every exact endpoint algorithm must evaluate all ten: incidence cardinality is not an information-based query lower bound, and algebraic dominance tests may discard locations without evaluating the root there.
